function: PPO policy allocates LEO satellite computing capacity and bandwidth to each satellite service group per slot; PSO and a coalition game, not learning, set intervals and groups (pp. 7-10).
system: LEO satellite (550 km, 250 MHz, 32 dBi) and RSUs (100 MHz, 10 dBi) serve CAVs; antennas given only as gains; carrier frequency not stated; no RIS (pp. 10-11).
method: PPO actor-critic reinforcement learning (MLP 128-128-64, ReLU), trained 1800 episodes of 8000 slots; the model-based PSO and coalition-game stage runs inside training (pp. 10-11).
data_channel: Custom simulator: LEO at 550 km, random CAV and RSU positions, stochastic CAV mobility, path-loss exponents 2.5 (satellite) and 3 (RSU); no fading model, dataset or measurements (pp. 10-11).
test_conditions: Trained 1800 episodes of 8000 slots, CAVs and RSUs reset randomly each episode; evaluated versus rural CAV density 10-30 and RSU density 1-5 per km2, reliability 0.95-0.99 (pp. 11-12).
baselines: Non-learned only: FCFS, random and average resource allocation; fixed-number satellite service groups by k-means with PPO allocation; no earlier learned method compared (pp. 11-12).
metrics: Overall resource cost (weighted computing and bandwidth usage of satellite and RSUs), reliability (probability of meeting the AoI threshold), training convergence of both (pp. 11-12).
complexity: O(L1 |X| (NU + L2 U M^2)) for the PSO and coalition-game stage only (p. 9); none for the PPO policy, only layer sizes (p. 11).
q1_support: p. 5: "is the channel gain". The channel gain is never specified beyond path-loss exponents 2.5 (satellite) and 3 (RSU) in Table III (p. 11); no 3GPP channel model, fading model, dataset or measured data.
q2_support: p. 11: "the performances of different resource allocation algorithms under different CAV densities in rural areas are shown in Fig. 5". The paper does not say that the trained policy was tested on conditions unseen in training, or retrained or fine-tuned for them.
q3_support: p. 11: "we adopt the following three benchmark algorithms for resource allocation, namely 1) FCFS-based allocation". Benchmarks are FCFS, random and average allocation (p. 11) and k-means partitions with PPO (p. 12); no earlier learned method is compared.
q4_support: p. 9: "the overall computational complexity for determining CAV partitions and sensing intervals for each SG is" O(L1 |X| (NU + L2 U M^2)); this covers only the PSO and coalition-game stage, with no complexity, parameter count or runtime for the PPO policy.
q5_support: p. 10: "CAVs and RSUs are randomly distributed in the area". Own simulation with parameters in Table III (p. 11); no code or data link, no public dataset, no measured data.
notes: Borderline above_phy: the PPO learns computing capacity (edge computing, above the physical layer) jointly with the bandwidth allocation of a LEO satellite, which passes through the clause that resource allocation in satellite links is physical layer; area 6 on that basis, reviewer to confirm. Sensing is infrastructure environment sensing whose data are processed and delivered, not radio sensing, so area 5 does not apply. Sensing interval and CAV partition are model-based (PSO, coalition game). q4 is 0 because the complexity analysis covers only that model-based stage; flip to 1 if the analysis of a non-learned component of the scheme counts.
